mappings.lean_concept: Hourly rows labelled by local New York bar start; a bar is complete at start + 1 hour; XNYS session membership over 2019-12-02 to 2020-04-30
mappings.engine_concept: Data with timestep 'hour' indexed at each row's bar END instant. A pure PandasData backtest derives its trading calendar from the supplied rows: each date's market open and close are its first and last index values (10:00 and 16:00 New York; 13:00 on 2019-12-24). Lifecycle hooks run on that calendar: before_market_opens at open minus 60 minutes, before_starting_trading at the open, on_trading_iteration every 60 minutes while the session is open, after_market_closes at the close.
mappings.decision: Data with timestep hour, indexed at each row's bar END instant (tz-aware). A pure PandasData backtest derives its trading calendar from the supplied rows (lumibot/strategies/strategy_executor.py 2630-2649), so each session is expected to span its first and last end-indexed rows (10:00 to 16:00 New York; 13:00 on 2019-12-24). No padding, forward fill or resampling. The declared short session is carried from the Nautilus manifest.
mappings.known_short_sessions_reason: 2019-12-24 is the XNYS Christmas Eve half day, closing at 13:00 New York, so it yields the 09:00, 10:00, 11:00 and 12:00 rows only. 104 sessions x 7 rows - 3 missing rows = 725.
evidence: lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/data_sources/pandas_data.py lines 160-188 (calendar from the first and last timestamp of each date)
lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/strategies/strategy_executor.py lines 2641-2649 (pure PandasData backtests use that calendar) and 2225-2454 (session setup, iteration loop and close lifecycle)
lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/backtesting/backtesting_broker.py lines 602-707 (time to close and open on that calendar)
mappings.validation: convert.check_sessions refuses any undeclared short or long session. The port checks that the engine's calendar equals the first and last end instant of each of the 104 converted sessions (guard sessions_from_rows) and that every lifecycle hook ran exactly at the preregistered clocks (guard lifecycle_clock).
limitations: Session membership comes from the retained daily file through convert.py; the engine applies no exchange calendar in this configuration.
Bundled history carries no original availability attestation, so event time is preserved but observation time is not independently attested.

mappings.lean_concept: A completed 16:00 bar may form an intent; the fill must land on a later session
mappings.engine_concept: after_market_closes runs at the session-final bar's end (16:00 New York). get_historical_prices(asset, 1, 'hour', timeshift=-1) at that clock returns the bar indexed 16:00, which with END-indexed bars is the completed decision bar; timeshift 0 would return the 15:00 bar. The port sizes from that bar's converted close and the engine-reported portfolio value and submits one GTC market order.
mappings.decision: The decision reads only the completed decision bar (end 16:00 New York) and submits after that instant; the order may fill only at the next session's first bar. check_decision_bar_is_session_final and check_causality apply, and the engine clock at submission is recorded.
mappings.decision_hook: after_market_closes, the preregistration's example hook, chosen before the first attempt and recorded in the port header and run.json. Post-hoc variants (failure_policy F5) may use before_market_opens or before_starting_trading.
evidence: tests/test_hour_timestep_support.py at 2dfdda100cdc34e5acb46a7f13e8208a35aede72 (sha256 820cd040c146faed010daacb08301b9c787aa7f269721391271b6af6b06bd6ac): a native hour request with timeshift=-1 includes the bar indexed at the requested instant
lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/entities/data.py lines 686-757 (last bar at or before the clock) and 1272-1299 (intraday slices end before that bar unless timeshift is negative)
probes/hook-probe.json (synthetic bars): the reads each hook sees
mappings.validation: fixture_strategy.check_decision_bar_is_session_final at each decision; a guard that the bar the engine returned has the decision bar's end instant and converted close; fixture_strategy.check_causality on the native fills; the engine clock at submission recorded beside each intent and required to be at or after the decision instant and before the fill (guard submission_clock).
limitations: The decision read proves which bar formed the intent. Whether the order then fills on a later session is decided by the engine's fill model; see market_on_open_proxy.

mappings.lean_concept: MarketOnOpenOrder filled by EquityFillModel.MarketOnOpenFill at the next session's first hourly bar OPEN, stamped at that bar's end (10:00 New York)
mappings.engine_concept: A market order with time_in_force 'gtc' submitted after the decision bar completes, filled by the backtesting broker at the open of the bar it selects and stamped with the broker clock.
mappings.decision: A GTC market order submitted after the decision bar completes is filled by the backtesting broker at the open of the bar it selects, stamped with the broker datetime (lumibot/backtesting/backtesting_broker.py 3091-3092 and the bar selection before it). With end-indexed bars the next session's first bar is indexed 10:00 New York. Code reading only; not documented in the pinned docs.
mappings.pre_run_finding: Contradicted on synthetic bars before the first attempt (probes/hook-probe.json). The backtesting broker processes pending orders at the current clock whenever the strategy awaits the next open, before the clock advances (backtesting_broker.py lines 665-707, reached from strategy_executor.py lines 1940-1970 right after after_market_closes). There it takes a two-bar window ending at the bar indexed at or before the clock (lines 2660-2691), selects the first bar indexed in [clock, clock + 2 hours] or else the latest bar at or before the clock, within one day (lines 2956-3080), and prices a market order at that bar's open (lines 3091-3092). With END-indexed bars the bar indexed at 16:00 is the decision bar itself, so the order fills at 16:00 at the decision bar's open. Hooks that submit before the next open (before_market_opens) fill at the same stale open whenever the gap is under a day, and only a submission at the next session's 10:00 (before_starting_trading) lands on the first bar's open, at the instant of submission. The status stays resolved because it is binding; the primary attempt runs the preregistered example hook and its verdict stands as scored.
evidence: lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/backtesting/backtesting_broker.py lines 665-707, 2067-2110, 2660-2691, 2956-3080 and 3091-3092
lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/strategies/strategy_executor.py lines 1940-1970 and 2318-2454
lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/backtesting/backtesting_broker.py lines 3483-3517 (a day time-in-force elapses at the session close or on a date change, so gtc is used)
probes/hook-probe.json (synthetic bars, three hooks, engine fill clock from the broker's trade-event log)
mappings.validation: The port reads every fill instant and price from the broker's trade-event log and checks placement at the next session's first bar end (guard fill_at_next_session_first_bar), the price against the open of the bar indexed at the fill instant, causality and the submission clock. compare.py compares price and instant against the oracle with zero tolerance.
limitations: Faithful to LEAN's MarketOnOpenFill only if the fill lands on the next session's first bar; the pre-run finding shows the engine does not do that for an order submitted at the decision bar's end.
PandasData has no opening-auction or at-the-open time-in-force in the pinned wheel; the documented raw timesteps are minute and day.

mappings.validation: The port checks the broker's trade-event log for any cash event (guard engine_cash_events) and the engine's own cash snapshots for any change other than fills (guard engine_cash_changes_only_at_fills). An engine dividend posting would replace the external entry for its ex-date with the engine's own amount and instant; the port never records both and never injects cash.

mappings.lean_concept: one_zero: zero fees, zero slippage. one_stress and later: 1 USD per order plus 20 bp adverse slippage with an explicit rounding stage
mappings.engine_concept: buy_trading_fees and sell_trading_fees empty and no slippage list, so the backtesting broker's trade cost is zero; the strategy updates cash in Decimal from the fill price and quantity and stores it as a float.
mappings.decision: Empty buy and sell trading-fee lists and no slippage. The port reads each native fill's cost back and records any nonzero value as a guard failure.
evidence: lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/backtesting/backtesting_broker.py lines 2032-2064 (trade cost is zero with no fee objects)
lumibot-4.6.1 wheel lumibot/strategies/_strategy.py lines 2120-2150 (cash update in Decimal, stored as float)

limitations: Zero-cost parity says nothing about the stressed cases' quantities or fill schedule.

blocked_extension.reason: The 1 USD per order and 20 bp adverse slippage mapping and the rounding stage for the stressed cases are not decided by this trial.

mappings.decision: Lumibot backtests track strategy cash from the budget; no margin model is configured or claimed. one_zero requests 1x, so no leverage, margin call or latch is exercised or claimed.

dependent_comparison_status.one_zero: market_on_open_proxy is resolved by binding but contradicted by the pre-run probe; distributions_and_cash is unsupported; margin_and_adaptive_state is blocked but not exercised at 1x

generated_id_normalization.rule: Only random identifiers are normalized: a uuid4 hex identifier (the Order default, lumibot/entities/order.py lines 24-27 and 479 in the wheel) is validated against ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ and replaced by its ordinal of first appearance in the run. The sequential identifiers the pinned Strategy.create_order assigns in backtests (bt_<n>, lumibot/strategies/strategy.py lines 884-890) are deterministic and stay raw, as ml4t's sequential ids do; any other shape is a guard failure. Published files carry order ordinals only.
generated_id_normalization.pre_run_finding: The preregistration expected uuid4 order identifiers. The port's mechanism probe on synthetic bars found bt_<n> identifiers for every backtest order, so in practice nothing is normalized.
